<!--
How to use this template

- Fill in every applicable section. Delete a section that does not apply rather
  than leaving it empty, and do not add top-level sections outside this
  template. Put design detail in Description or Requirements, and record
  decisions made after the issue was filed in a comment.
- Keep the written body under roughly 1500 characters and 30 lines, not
  counting section headings. Go over only when the issue is genuinely complex.
- Link related issues and pull requests by number, for example `#123`. Do not
  use vague pointers such as "previous work" or "remaining changes". Do not
  cite any document as context, including plans, reviews, scratch notes, and
  committed design specs; restate the relevant point in the body.
- Description: say what is missing or wrong today, and why it matters.
  Do not restate the title.
- Scope is optional: name the service(s), surface(s), and target(s) when the
  request is specific to them. Surface means where in the UI it applies, such as
  a browse row, hover preview, search grid, or settings panel. For an internal
  refactor, name the affected modules instead. Delete the section otherwise.
- Requirements are acceptance criteria, one per plain `-` bullet, phrased so
  each can be verified and ending with a period. Never use a task list
  (`- [ ]` or `- [x]`): issues are not progress checklists, and a closed issue
  with unchecked boxes misreports its state. Keep them implementation-agnostic:
  say what must be true, not which file changes. Naming a module or symbol is
  allowed when the issue is itself an internal refactor; also state the
  behavior that must not change.
- Do not add a requirement that a CI command passes. CI already enforces the
  merge gates; put command output and test notes in the pull request.
- Open Questions is optional: keep it for decisions you want input on before
  work starts, and delete the section when there are none. Do not write "None."
-->
